description: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of various media outlets, representing their relative proportions within a dataset related to political discourse. The chart is divided into 18 distinct slices, with text labels positioned outside the perimeter and numerical values displayed directly inside each corresponding segment. There is no separate legend, and none of the slices are visually emphasized through explosion, offsetting, or bolding. Visually, the segments are arranged in a counter-clockwise direction in a generally descending order of size, beginning with the largest individual outlet and concluding with an aggregated category. The specific slices, in counter-clockwise order, include Breitbart (blue, 14), Drudge Report (orange, 8), The Daily Caller (green, 8), The Huffington Post (red, 7), NPR (purple, 6), Vox (brown, 6), The Guardian (pink, 5), BBC (grey, 5), RT (olive green, 4), Daily Kos (cyan, 3), National Review (dark blue, 3), Daily Mail (orange, 3), Red State (green, 3), Fox News (red, 3), CNN (purple, 3), PoliticusUSA (brown, 3), and Shareblue (pink, 3). The chart is completed by a large grey slice labeled "Other," which contains a value of 13 and is positioned between Shareblue and Breitbart.
